newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S&P assigns AA+ rating to Stockholm EMTN programme.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns AA+ rating to Stockholm EMTN programme.

text.p: U.S. credit rating agency Standard & Poor's (S&P) said on Tuesday it had assigned an AA+ rating to a City of Stockholm $1 billion Euro Medium Term Note (EMTN) programme, outlook negative.
"The rating outlook is negative reflecting the negative outlook of the Kingdom of Sweden's foreign currency debt," S&P said in a statement.
The agency also affirmed the city's longterm local currency rating of AA+ and shortterm ratings of A-1+ and K-1 with the outlook stable.
"The ratings reflect Stockholm's strong and well diversified local economy but also its modest and, in 1996, weakened financial performance," the agency said.
"Further the ratings reflect the city's low tax-supported debt, although total public sector debt is high."
The city has a tax-supported debt of around 55 percent of revenues which is reasonably low by international standards.
S&P said the local currency outlook of stable assumed continued efforts to keep a restrictive expenditure policy, despite financial pressure from the social security field.
"In combination with a growing tax base this will help the city keep debt levels stable," it said.
